findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders for every delivery method
findings.body: The `retryCount > 1` branch is not constrained to `WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This endpoint will therefore delete any `WorkflowReminder` with more than one retry, including a future email or WhatsApp reminder, even though the retry behavior being implemented is for SMS scheduling. Keep `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` in the retry-exhaustion branch (and ensure it only targets the intended unscheduled state) so shared reminder records cannot be removed by this SMS cron.

findings.title: Retry count updates lose failures when cron invocations overlap
findings.body: The retry count is calculated from the value read by `findMany` and then written back. If two authorized cron invocations select the same unscheduled reminder, both can observe (for example) `retryCount = 0`, both attempt scheduling, and both write `1`; the row is then retried again despite already having failed twice. The same overlap can cause multiple scheduling attempts for one reminder. Claim the reminder/attempt atomically with a conditional update or lock, and increment in the database rather than writing a stale value.

findings.title: Reminders with no usable destination are never counted as failed
findings.body: Failure accounting is entirely inside the `if (message?.length && sendTo)` block. When an SMS reminder has an empty or missing recipient number (or no generated message), the loop silently skips it without setting `scheduled` or incrementing `retryCount`, so the cron continues selecting it until its scheduled date. This leaves a class of invalid SMS reminders with the exact indefinite rescheduling behavior the retry limit is intended to stop; treat an unusable destination/message as a terminal or retryable failure and update/delete the reminder accordingly.
